Q: How do budgets, stop reasons and authoritative tool state keep an agent loop bounded?
A: An agent harness owns invocation, tool dispatch, state updates and termination. Bound steps, elapsed time, tool concurrency and spend under a shared run contract rather than a separate unlimited budget for every child call. A model's claim that it is finished is distinct from confirmed task completion. Record the stop reason and any accepted work still in progress. Stop repeated invalid proposals instead of repairing forever, and check policy at the effect boundary even after a plausible plan has passed review.
Why: A tool times out after accepting a job and the agent proposes another job. The harness should reconcile the accepted operation instead of spending its remaining steps creating duplicate work.
Risk: A step limit can stop generation while leaving accepted external work unresolved.
Trade: Bounded autonomy makes resource use explicit but still needs a recovery policy.
Try: Test success, denied tool, exhausted budget and unknown accepted-operation outcomes.
